title: ChatGPT skips the middle of your message #shorts
description:
Stanford moved one paragraph around inside the same prompt, and the score moved with it. Models use what sits at the start and the end of a message. The middle is where things go missing.

In the worst case in that paper, thirty documents in the prompt scored LOWER than giving the model no documents at all (closed-book, 56.1%).

Chroma then tested eighteen models the same way. Every one degraded as the input grew, and it starts long before any context window is full.

Two things to try tonight:
- Paste the paragraph, not the whole file.
- Put your question underneath the material, not above it.

Sources:
Liu, Lin, Hewitt, Paranjape, Bevilacqua, Petroni, Liang - "Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts" (Stanford / UC Berkeley / Samaya AI): https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172
Chroma Research - "Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance": https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot
Xia, Wang, Huang, Liu - "Diagnosing and Mitigating Context Rot in Long-horizon Search": https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29718
